Why AbarVa is different from a raw LLM

Raw models can draft a plausible strategy memo. AbarVa creates a controlled system around the decision: context intake, evidence state, use-case map, architecture path, Source option, value ledger, and named human approval.

Raw LLM pattern

  • Plausible answer with weak enterprise memory.
  • Limited visibility into source gaps or approvals.
  • No native owner, stage gate, value ledger, or sourcing trail.

AbarVa pattern

  • Context, corpus, uploaded evidence, and approval queue first.
  • Sentinel surfaces the decision and gaps; Maestro turns it into execution.
  • Tower tracks value, risk, dependencies, and human governance.

Proof vignette 1: Which AI bets should move first?

The CDAO does not need another generic use-case list. AbarVa turns the portfolio into a decision landscape: what is in flight, what is blocked, which foundations unlock multiple bets, and where executive action should land.

Value to land: avoid AI failure by picking bets that have value, feasible data foundations, clear sponsors, and an execution path.

Sentinel executive brief. The screenshot deliberately shows AI draft and review-before-acting controls.

The Map turns AI opportunities into dependency, risk, owner, and sequencing logic.

Talk track

For a Meridian / PHS-style modernization program, AbarVa should help leadership choose the right first moves: population health, Stars / quality, chronic disease, avoidable utilization, payment integrity, care-management productivity, and data-platform foundations.

The output is not "AI says yes." It is a reviewed recommendation with evidence keys, gaps, owners, and a required approval action.

Proof vignette 2: Context layer prevents false confidence

The context layer is where AbarVa becomes sticky. It captures the client's systems, data domains, KPIs, initiatives, vendors, rate cards, architecture patterns, evidence, approval state, and gap list.

Important truth: the current walkthrough shows internal context not fully loaded and citation-gap warnings. That is not a cosmetic flaw; it is the readiness signal that prevents pretending.

Setup/Admin context-layer overview from production.

Approval and embedding queue: evidence must be onboarded and governed before reliance.

Enterprise Context gap: AbarVa does not pretend private context exists before it is loaded.

Proof vignette 3: Strategy becomes architecture, business case, mobilization

AbarVa turns selected AI bets into Strategic Moves: target architecture, data and integration needs, governance, human-in-the-loop design, roadmap, business case, mobilization plan, and value tracking.

Source stays optional in the first CDAO motion. It becomes a day-2 expansion lane when the client needs to pick a Databricks implementation partner, managed services provider, analytics SI, or custom product-development team.

Moves portfolio: the bridge from strategy to execution governance.

Tower: value, dependencies, status, and executive governance.

Where the economics show up

The value case should include AI failure avoidance, better use-case selection, optimized human/agent mix, reduced SI assessment spend, vendor cost optimization, and a tighter 90-day mobilization plan.

Use baseline and forecast only until realized-value evidence exists. That keeps the page aggressive on value while still being responsible.

AbarVa gives the CDAO a governed way to say yes, no, or not yet.

It helps leadership decide what to do, why it is worth doing, what evidence supports it, what architecture and execution model it requires, what should be sourced, and who must approve the next move.

Boundary: this proof uses live AbarVa screenshots and a synthetic Meridian demo inspired by public PHS context. It does not claim confidential PHS data, realized savings, or production private-data-plane completeness.
